title: Which volcano produced the sulfate deposit dated to around 1809?
short: Ice cores and observations of a high-altitude haze point to a major eruption. A disputed date complicates one lead from Java.
matters: An identified volcano would improve estimates of the eruption’s timing and geographic reach. It would also help distinguish its climate effects from other events in the decade before and after Tambora.
stuck: An 1836 account dates a Lamongan eruption to December 1808. Its cited Latin source dates the event to November 1818. The discrepancy leaves open whether separate evidence supports an eruption in 1808.
solved: Link independently dated source evidence to the ice-core event, ideally with volcanic glass that can be matched to a candidate.
approach: Find the earliest witnesses for each Lamongan date and search independent Java records for reports of ash, darkness or ground shaking. Compare the timing with South American observations.

existing.title: Ice core evidence for an explosive tropical volcanic eruption 6 years preceding Tambora

existing.authors: A. Guevara-Murua, C. A. Williams, E. J. Hendy, A. C. Rust and K. V. Cashman
existing.title: Observations of a stratospheric aerosol veil from a tropical volcanic eruption in December 1808: is this the Unknown ~1809 eruption?
existing.note: Identified the reports of Francisco José de Caldas in Bogotá (a veil dimming the sun from 11 December 1808) and José Hipólito Unanue in Lima (abnormal twilights) as aerosol observations, and proposed an eruption date of about 4 December 1808.

existing.authors: Claudia Timmreck, Matthew Toohey, Davide Zanchettin, Stefan Brönnimann et al.
existing.title: The unidentified eruption of 1809: a climatic cold case
existing.note: Reviewed the ice-core, instrumental and documentary evidence and modelled the climatic effects, concluding that the source, season and exact year of the eruption remain unknown.
